frontier.note: SECURITY. Closes three trust-boundary defects, all reachable over PostgREST without this application. (A) request_kind='employer_attestation' could name a CLAIM: a holder could open an employer attestation against a regulated credential such as VU1 and an owner/admin of the target employer could approve it, producing a state-regulated guard qualification 'verified' by a company with no standing to say so. Now refused at three points -- a new CHECK constraint sp_vr_employer_attestation_is_employment_only on sp_verification_requests (period_id NOT NULL AND claim_id IS NULL), a guard in sp_submit_for_verification, and a guard in sp_verifier_decide so a row written BEFORE this migration still cannot be turned into trust. (B) sp_verifier_decide accepted decision='approved' with verification_method NULL; only the TypeScript layer refused it, and that layer is skippable. Now refused in the function. WHICH methods are allowed is not restated: the existing sp_verification_requests.verification_method CHECK remains the model. (C) sp_verifier_decide read the request's status and then wrote with no lock across the gap, so two concurrent deciders could both pass the already-decided check and both write. The SELECT now takes FOR UPDATE on that one row, and a partial unique index sp_vd_one_final_decision_per_request makes 'one final decision per request' an invariant of the data (excludes clarification_requested, which is not final, and revoked, which is filed against the approving request on purpose). Two partial unique indexes sp_vr_one_open_request_per_claim / _per_period do the same for the matching submission race; sp_submit_for_verification maps the resulting unique violation back to SP_REQUEST_ALREADY_OPEN. Creates no table and no column, adds no workflow state, no assertion level and no verification method, and does not touch sp_is_verifier. Introduces no object the application calls, so it does not gate the application release it ships with. Rewrites no data: each new invariant is checked against existing rows in a preflight DO block that refuses with the offending identifiers rather than being added NOT VALID.
